To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The visual realism of virtual humans is important in determining participant responses to them, however it is not the only determinant of participant response.
1. The quality of the body movement of a virtual human has a strong effect on the emotional response of participants in immersive virtual environ­ ments.
the behavioural model used to portray the psychological state of the virtual humans has a significant impact on the responses from the participants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of virtual humans on people.
the impact of the behaviour of virtual agents in immersive environments.
the impact of nonverbal cues in virtual humans in immersive virtual environments and how these can be used in applications such as training and therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
virtual human behaviour has an effect on the responses of participants in immersive virtual envi­ ronments.
the quality of the virtual humans behaviour has a significant effect on participant responses and this is not dependent on the level of realism in the virtual humans appearance.

the quality and complexity of behaviour displayed in virtual humans can affect the responses of participants in immersive virtual envi­ ronments to the extent that they are able to evoke the same responses observed in the real world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the behavioural cues used by real humans to convey a psychological state are similar to those used by virtual humans.
the quality of body movements is important for portraying psychological states in virtual humans and that this is more important than the visual appearance of the virtual human.

virtual humans with a high degree of behavioural complexity and a high degree of visual fidelity can be used in immersive virtual environments to portray psychological states and evoke responses that are similar to the real world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to design a virtual human that can be used in an IVE for the purpose of eliciting participant responses that are similar to that of the physical world.
virtual humans can be designed to have significant effects on the responses of participants in immersive virtual environ­ ments.
virtual human models can be effective in IVEs, provided that they have the right behaviours and the right level of complexity.
